scenario.description: A manufacturing engineering manager must authorize and configure a controlled production run using an alternate medical-grade resin for Line 6, with input from quality, process engineering, regulatory affairs, and production planning.

shared_context.S1: Line 6 is scheduled to make 1,400 medical-device housings this week, but the normally approved resin R-17 is temporarily unavailable.
shared_context.S2: An alternate medical-grade resin, R-22, is available for a controlled run on Line 6.
shared_context.S3: The normal change-control process requires a documented engineering authorization before production with an alternate material.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the final authorization and configuration decision.
shared_context.S5: As part of the routine change-control review, Elena asks quality, process engineering, regulatory affairs, and production planning for any constraints before issuing the authorization.

PF1.text: Ravi checked the customer's revised control plan this morning and confirmed that an alternate-resin run requires dimensional and tensile testing on exactly 50 first-off housings, with all 50 passing before the run can be released, plus retention of exactly 10 samples; the revised plan has not yet been attached to the change-control record.

PF2.text: Mei's process trial showed that R-22 must be dried at 80 degrees Celsius for exactly 4 hours and requires a 45-minute screw purge before molding; she recorded the trial in her engineering notebook but has not entered it into the production setup sheet.

PF3.text: Jonas confirmed with the resin manufacturer that the medical-grade declaration applies only to supplier lot L2407-18, and regulatory procedure requires lot-specific traceability and customer notification before any housings made from that lot are shipped; the supplier confirmation is still in his email rather than the release file.

PF4.text: Carla's updated capacity check shows that Friday's available Line 6 window is exactly 15.5 machine hours; after the required setup, the line can produce 100 housings per hour, so the authorized run quantity must be exactly 1,400 housings rather than the full nominal order quantity; she has not yet posted the revised capacity sheet.

acceptance_conditions: The alternate run must be authorized using R-22 from lot L2407-18.
The authorized quantity must be exactly 1,400 housings.
R-22 must be dried at 80 degrees Celsius for exactly 4 hours.
The screw purge must be exactly 45 minutes.
Exactly 50 first-off housings must receive the required testing before release.
Customer notification must occur before shipment and lot traceability must be recorded.
The customer's revised control-plan requirement must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The exact customer control plan changes the first-off requirement to 50 tested housings and 10 retained samples, and it supplies the required justification.
The process trial changes the setup from an ordinary material changeover to exactly 4 hours of drying at 80 degrees Celsius and a 45-minute screw purge.
The manufacturer confirmation changes the approved material assignment to lot L2407-18 and adds mandatory pre-shipment customer notification and lot traceability.
The exact 15.5-hour machine window and 100-housings-per-hour rate change the authorized production quantity to exactly 1,400 housings.
